title: ENEA and two universities test machine-learning forecasts of heatwave-driven grid failures in Italy
summary: ENEA and two Italian universities tested a machine-learning model that forecasts grid failures during heatwaves; ENEA's announcement of 18 May 2023 reports no avoided outage.
account: ENEA, Politecnico di Bari and Università Roma Tre tested machine-learning forecasts of heatwave-related failures in a large distribution grid in southern Italy. ENEA's announcement of 18 May 2023 says that training used failures from 2015 to 2020, temperature, humidity and energy flows, followed by tests on unseen inputs. The researchers proposed that operators use the forecasts for corrective maintenance. The announcement reports neither a named utility deployment nor an avoided outage. ENEA's Maria Valenti said that most failures in the studied network occurred at cable joints. The study appeared in IEEE Transactions on Industry Applications in 2023 under the title "A Machine Learning Approach to Fault Prediction of Power Distribution Grids under Heatwaves." In 2025 a Politecnico di Milano team tested similar forecasts on the Milan distribution network. The authors of the Italian study posted a copy of the paper on TechRxiv on 7 October 2025. No source reports that the grid operator or any other utility adopted the model.
purpose: The system was built to forecast heatwave-related failures on electricity networks so that operators can act in advance. The sources document development and testing only.
